issues.legal_issue: A lease that demises land and requires the lessee to build on it does not also demise the building unless the instrument, properly construed, includes the building in the demise.
material_facts: The lease schedule described a parcel of land, and the lessees agreed to construct a building on it at their expense.
The lease contained no express term stating that the building was included in the demise or that ownership of it passed to the lessors while the lease continued.
The lessees agreed to surrender the land and building at the end of the lease without compensation for the building.
issues.conclusion: The lease demised only the land. The building remained the lessees’ property while the lease subsisted, and the covenant to surrender it without compensation did not make it part of the demise; after expiry, the lessors were entitled to the building.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the Indian rule that there is no absolute rule that a building affixed to land becomes part of the land and subject to the same ownership rights. It relied on Narayan Das Khettry v. Jatindra Nath Roy Chowdhury and Vallabhdas Naranji v. Development Officer, Bandra, and considered section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act, which permits a lessee to remove structures before the lease expires absent a contrary contract. A lessee may contract to surrender a building without compensation, but that agreement does not by itself transfer ownership during the lease or establish that the building was demised.

rule.if: lease_interpretation_proceeding and lease_identifies_only_land and lessee_builds_structure and no_term_includes_structure_in_demise and surrender_without_compensation

predicates.lease_interpretation_proceeding: The dispute requires a court to construe a lease concerning land and a structure built on it.
predicates.lease_identifies_only_land: The lease describes the land as the property demised without identifying the structure as part of that property.
predicates.lessee_builds_structure: The lease requires or permits the lessee to build a structure on the land.
predicates.no_term_includes_structure_in_demise: The lease contains no term stating that the structure is included in the demise.
predicates.surrender_without_compensation: The lessee agrees to surrender the structure at the end of the lease without compensation.
predicates.building_not_included_in_demise: The structure is not included in the property demised by the lease.

issues.definition: When a lease-construction proceeding concerns a lease identifying only land, under which the lessee builds a structure and agrees to surrender it without compensation, but no term includes the structure in the demise, the structure is not included in the demise.

issues.legal_issue: Rent-control protection for a tenant who remains in possession after a fixed-term lease expires does not continue the lease beyond its agreed term.
material_facts: The land lease was for a fixed term that had expired.
The lessees remained in possession without the lessors’ consent and claimed protection under rent-control legislation.

The lessors sought possession of the building under the surrender covenant, while accepting that the lessees had statutory protection against eviction from the land except as permitted by the legislation.
issues.conclusion: The legislation did not continue the lease beyond its fixed term. It gave the occupants who remained in possession statutory-tenant status and protection against eviction from the land, but did not prevent enforcement of the separate covenant concerning the building.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the rent-control legislation protected a person who remained in possession after the lease ended, but did not extend the lease term. The statutory tenant could not be evicted from the land except in accordance with the legislation; that protection did not convert the expired lease into a continuing contractual lease or determine rights in a building that was not demised.

rule.if: post_expiry_rent_control_proceeding and fixed_term_lease_expired and tenant_remains_without_landlord_consent and rent_control_protects_occupancy

predicates.post_expiry_rent_control_proceeding: The proceeding concerns rent-control protection claimed after a fixed-term lease has expired.
predicates.fixed_term_lease_expired: The agreed fixed term of the lease has ended.
predicates.tenant_remains_without_landlord_consent: The tenant continues in possession after expiry without the landlord’s consent.
predicates.rent_control_protects_occupancy: The applicable rent-control regime protects the tenant’s continued occupation against eviction except on specified grounds.
predicates.statutory_occupancy_protection_does_not_: Statutory protection against eviction does not continue the expired contractual lease.

issues.definition: When a fixed-term lease has expired, the tenant remains without the landlord’s consent, and rent control protects continued occupancy, that protection does not extend the lease term.

issues.legal_issue: An owner entitled to a building after expiry of a lease may claim rents and profits from that building even if the owner cannot enter the land without the land occupant’s consent.
material_facts: The lessors were entitled to the building after the lease expired, and the building had been let to other occupants.
The lessees remained statutory tenants of the land and argued that the lessors could not collect the building’s rents without entering the land.
The lessors sought a declaration of their right to the building’s rents and profits, not a declaration granting a right to enter the land.
issues.conclusion: The lessors were entitled to the rents and profits from the building. Their inability to enter the land without consent did not bar a declaration of that right, and the occupants were restrained from interfering with collection of the rents and profits.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished a declaration of entitlement to rents and profits from a right to enter the land. Because the requested declaration did not assert a right of entry, the occupants’ control of access to the land was no valid legal objection to granting it.

rule.if: building_rent_claim_proceeding and claimant_owns_building_after_lease and building_is_rented_to_occupants and claim_does_not_seek_land_entry

predicates.building_rent_claim_proceeding: The proceeding includes a claim to rents or profits from a building.
predicates.claimant_owns_building_after_lease: The claimant is entitled to the building after the lease has expired.
predicates.building_is_rented_to_occupants: The building has been let to occupants who receive or control its rents.
predicates.claim_does_not_seek_land_entry: The claim seeks entitlement to building rents or profits rather than a right to enter the land.
predicates.building_owner_may_claim_building_rents_: The building owner may claim its rents and profits without thereby obtaining a right to enter the land.

issues.definition: When a claimant entitled to a building after lease expiry seeks its rents from occupants but does not seek entry onto the land, the claimant may claim those rents without a right of land entry.

issues.legal_issue: A suit may proceed without the legal representatives of a deceased joint lessee where they are not necessary to determine the relief sought.
material_facts: One person sued as a representative of a joint lessee had died before the suit began, and that person’s legal representatives were not added to the record.
The claim for accounts of rents was directed only against the defendant who effectively controlled the building and received its rents.
The omitted person and representatives had not taken an active role concerning the building, and the requested declaration could be granted in their absence.
issues.conclusion: The suit could not be dismissed for non-joinder because the absent legal representatives were not necessary parties to the relief sought.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the necessary-party principle by considering the nature of the relief and whether it could be granted in the absence of the omitted representatives. It noted the concession made at trial that the suit could not be dismissed merely for this non-joinder and concluded that the omitted representatives were not necessary parties. No earlier case or specific statutory provision was relied on for this ruling.

predicates.civil_suit_proceeding: The matter is a civil suit seeking relief concerning property or its income.
predicates.deceased_joint_lessee_representatives_om: The legal representatives of a deceased joint lessee have not been joined to the suit.
predicates.omitted_representatives_not_controlling_: The omitted representatives do not effectively control the property or the dispute about the relief sought.
predicates.relief_determinable_without_them: The court can determine and grant the requested relief without the omitted representatives.
predicates.suit_not_dismissed_for_nonjoinder: The suit is not dismissed solely because those representatives were not joined.

issues.definition: When representatives of a deceased joint lessee are omitted, do not control the dispute, and the requested relief can be determined without them, the suit is not dismissed for non-joinder.
